correctness.rationale: A finite near-norm block can be translated simultaneously on rows and columns into infinitely many disjoint copies while preserving both the relative pattern and the symbol. Singular values concatenate, giving an exact \(\ell_p\) or \(c_0\) subspace on which \(T\) is a scalar multiple of an isometry. This directly yields the Bernstein and strict-singularity distances; finite-codimension intersection gives Gelfand numbers, finite-rank comparison gives approximation numbers, and escaping rectangular compressions give Kolmogorov numbers and Hausdorff noncompactness. The argument also works at \(p=\infty\) because the ambient ideal is compact operators.
